research_question: Can a transdiagnostic, mechanism-guided, adaptive care system improve treatment matching and durability for heterogeneous psychiatric presentations?

primary_direction.name: Mechanism-Guided Adaptive Psychiatry
primary_direction.thesis: More effective care will come from repeated, clinician-supervised inference over symptom dimensions, multimodal mechanism profiles, and treatment-response trajectories rather than from diagnosis-only classification.
primary_direction.novelty: A nested, mechanism-aware model links transdiagnostic phenotypes to modality-specific treatment response and uses time-varying evidence for safe adaptation.
predictions: Multimodal dimensional models will improve held-out trajectory calibration.
Inflammation-dysconnectivity strata will moderate response for a subset rather than all patients.
Repeated early-response signals will improve treatment-switch timing.
Clinical utility gains will shrink under missing modalities but remain above diagnosis-only baselines if uncertainty is modeled.
falsifiers: No out-of-sample gain over diagnosis-only baseline.
Mechanism strata do not moderate response after leakage controls.
Adaptive policy does not improve utility in prospective emulation.
Calibration or subgroup fairness degrades beyond predefined limits.

identity.topic: complex mental disorder diagnosis and treatment
